window.__JAE_PAYLOAD__=D;window.__JAE_VIEWS__={};

/* ===== view: explorer (from template.html) ===== */
(function(){
var VIEWROOT = document.getElementById('view-explorer');
var VIEWID = function(id){ return VIEWROOT.querySelector('#' + id) || document.getElementById('explorer-reference').querySelector('#' + id); };
const DATA = window.__JAE_PAYLOAD__;

/* ---------- typed-array helpers ---------- */
function unb64(s, Type){
  const bin = atob(s); const buf = new ArrayBuffer(bin.length);
  const v = new Uint8Array(buf);
  for(let i=0;i<bin.length;i++) v[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
  return new Type(buf);
}
function deq(codes, lo, hi, max){ // integer codes -> floats
  const out = new Float32Array(codes.length); const s=(hi-lo)/max;
  for(let i=0;i<codes.length;i++) out[i]=lo+codes[i]*s;
  return out;
}
/* Colours come from the shared token reader: it caches the live declaration and
   falls back from a legacy name to its canonical one, so this view keeps every
   css('--ink3')-style call it already had while the values follow the master. */
const css = n => PC.css(n);

/* ---------- decode payload ---------- */
const D = DATA;
const NC = D.cells.n;
const cellType = unb64(D.cells.cell_type, Uint8Array);
const cellBatch = unb64(D.cells.batch, Uint8Array);
const heldout = unb64(D.cells.heldout, Uint8Array);
const globalIdx = unb64(D.cells.index, Uint32Array);
const sScore = deq(unb64(D.cells.S.data, Uint16Array), D.cells.S.lo, D.cells.S.hi, 65535);
const gScore = deq(unb64(D.cells.G2M.data, Uint16Array), D.cells.G2M.lo, D.cells.G2M.hi, 65535);
const pTime  = deq(unb64(D.cells.pseudotime.data, Uint16Array), -1, 1, 65535);
const MAT = unb64(D.matrix.data, Uint8Array);
const NCOL = D.matrix.shape[1];
const topIdx = unb64(D.top_genes.idx, Uint16Array);
const topVal = deq(unb64(D.top_genes.val, Uint8Array), D.top_genes.lo, D.top_genes.hi, 255);
const NTOP = D.top_genes.shape[1];
const LAT = D.latent && D.latent.data ? deq(unb64(D.latent.data, Uint8Array), D.latent.lo, D.latent.hi, 255) : null;
const LATD = D.latent && D.latent.shape ? D.latent.shape[1] : 0;

const coordCache = {};
function coordsOf(v){
  if(coordCache[v]) return coordCache[v];
  const c = D.coords[v];
  if(!c) return null;
  const x = deq(unb64(c.x, Uint16Array), c.sx[0], c.sx[1], 65535);
  const y = deq(unb64(c.y, Uint16Array), c.sy[0], c.sy[1], 65535);
  return coordCache[v] = {x,y};
}

const lineageOf = D.cell_type_lineage;
/* The seven lineages take --series-1..6 and --muted, in this fixed order — the
   suite's categorical ramp, read at draw time so a theme flip re-colours them. */
const LINEAGE_TOKEN = ['--series-1','--series-3','--series-5','--series-2',
                       '--series-6','--series-4','--muted'];
const LINCOL = {};
function refreshLineageColours(){
  D.lineage_order.forEach((l,k)=> LINCOL[l] = css(LINEAGE_TOKEN[k % LINEAGE_TOKEN.length]));
}
refreshLineageColours();
/* nine donor batches over the suite's eight categorical series plus --muted,
   read at draw time so they follow the theme */
const BATCH_TOKEN = ['--series-1','--series-2','--series-3','--series-4','--series-5',
                     '--series-6','--series-7','--series-8','--muted'];
let BATCHCOL = [];
function refreshBatchColours(){ BATCHCOL = BATCH_TOKEN.map(css); }
refreshBatchColours();

/* ---------- canvas plumbing — the SHARED runtime ----------
   Sizing goes through PC.fit (DPR-aware, capped at 2x, clears, returns the ctx),
   so this demo no longer carries its own DPR maths. Two details this wrapper
   still owns, because PC.fit cannot know them:

   1. The AUTHORED css height, cached on the node the first time it is read.
      `cv.height = …` reflects into the `height` CONTENT ATTRIBUTE, so re-reading
      that attribute returns what the previous draw wrote and the height gets
      multiplied by dpr on every redraw. That was the bitmap explosion reported
      on cv-scree (240 → 960 → 3840 → … → 245760 at dpr 2) — invisible at 1x.
   2. PC.fit writes cv.style.width, and `#view-explorer canvas{width:100%}` is
      then out-competed by that inline value, so a LATER measurement of
      cv.clientWidth returns the frozen width and the canvas can never shrink.
      Clearing the inline width before measuring is the documented workaround
      (the phone chart overlay does the same thing for the same reason). */
function fit(cv){
  const h = cv.__pcCssH !== undefined ? cv.__pcCssH
          : (cv.__pcCssH = +cv.getAttribute('height'));
  cv.style.width = "";
  const w = cv.clientWidth || (cv.parentElement && cv.parentElement.clientWidth) || 220;
  const g = PC.fit(cv, w, h);
  return {g,w,h};
}
/* One tooltip contract for every panel in this view: nearest point through the
   shared hit-tester, readout through the shared #tip. `onClick` must be present
   on the FIRST PC.hover call for a canvas — `if (st.bound) return` runs before
   the click binding — so every caller passes its opts every draw and the first
   one wins. */
function bindHover(cv, pts, html, opts){
  return PC.hover(cv, pts, Object.assign({
    onHit: (i, evt) => PC.tip(html(i), evt),
    onLeave: () => PC.hideTip()
  }, opts || {}));
}
function txt(g,s,x,y,{size=11,col=null,align='left',baseline='alphabetic',weight=400}={}){
  g.fillStyle = col || css('--ink3');
  /* the family comes from the --font token via the shared reader, so a suite-level
     type change reaches this view's canvas labels too */
  g.font = weight+' '+size+'px '+PC.font.family();
  g.textAlign = align; g.textBaseline = baseline; g.fillText(s,x,y);
}
function line(g,x1,y1,x2,y2,col,w=1){
  g.strokeStyle=col; g.lineWidth=w; g.beginPath(); g.moveTo(x1,y1); g.lineTo(x2,y2); g.stroke();
}

/* ---------- state ---------- */
const state = {
  cell: 0,
  col: 0,
  lineage: '',
  color: 'lineage',
  variant: 'jae_full',
};

/* ================= STAGE 1: design matrix bridge ================= */
const MX_ROWS = 150;           // rows drawn in the schematic
let mxRows = [];               // display-sample indices shown as matrix rows
function pickMatrixRows(){
  const pool = [];
  for(let i=0;i<NC;i++){
    if(state.lineage && lineageOf[cellType[i]] !== state.lineage) continue;
    pool.push(i);
  }
  if(!pool.length) return [];
  // sort by cell type so the heatmap has visible structure, then subsample evenly
  pool.sort((a,b)=> cellType[a]-cellType[b] || a-b);
  const step = pool.length / Math.min(MX_ROWS, pool.length);
  const out=[];
  for(let k=0;k<Math.min(MX_ROWS,pool.length);k++) out.push(pool[Math.floor(k*step)]);
  if(!out.includes(state.cell) && (!state.lineage || lineageOf[cellType[state.cell]]===state.lineage)){
    out[Math.floor(out.length/2)] = state.cell;
    out.sort((a,b)=> cellType[a]-cellType[b] || a-b);
  }
  return out;
}
const mxGeom = {};
function drawMatrix(){

  const cv = VIEWID('cv-matrix');
  const {g,w,h} = fit(cv);
  mxRows = pickMatrixRows();
  const padL=8, padR=118, padT=30, padB=30;
  const cw = (w-padL-padR)/NCOL, ch = (h-padT-padB)/Math.max(mxRows.length,1);
  mxGeom.padL=padL; mxGeom.padT=padT; mxGeom.cw=cw; mxGeom.ch=ch; mxGeom.n=mxRows.length;

  // heat cells
  const heat = PC.rampScale();          // resolve the 5 ramp stops once per draw
  for(let r=0;r<mxRows.length;r++){
    const ci = mxRows[r], base = ci*NCOL;
    for(let c=0;c<NCOL;c++){
      const v = MAT[base+c]/255;
      if(v<=0.012) continue;
      /* the suite's sequential ramp; alpha stays the density cue */
      g.globalAlpha = 0.10+0.90*Math.min(1,v*1.5);
      g.fillStyle = heat(Math.min(1,v*1.5));
      g.fillRect(padL+c*cw, padT+r*ch, Math.max(cw,0.6), Math.max(ch,0.9));
    }
  }
  g.globalAlpha=1;
  // gene | protein divider
  const nGene = D.column_kind.filter(k=>k==='gene').length;
  line(g, padL+nGene*cw, padT-6, padL+nGene*cw, padT+mxRows.length*ch+4, css('--line2'),1);
  txt(g,'← '+nGene+' marker genes', padL+nGene*cw-4, padT-11,{size:10,align:'right'});
  txt(g,'134 proteins →', padL+nGene*cw+4, padT-11,{size:10});

  // selected column
  const cx = padL+state.col*cw;
  g.strokeStyle = css('--matrix-column'); g.lineWidth=1.6;
  g.strokeRect(cx-0.5, padT-3, Math.max(cw,2)+1, mxRows.length*ch+6);
  txt(g,'X[:,j]', cx+Math.max(cw,2)/2, h-padB+30,{size:10,col:css('--matrix-column'),align:'center'});

  // selected row
  const rpos = mxRows.indexOf(state.cell);
  if(rpos>=0){
    const ry = padT+rpos*ch;
    g.strokeStyle = css('--matrix-row'); g.lineWidth=1.6;
    g.strokeRect(padL-3, ry-0.5, (w-padL-padR)+6, Math.max(ch,2)+1);
    txt(g,'X[i,:]', padL-5, ry+Math.max(ch,2)/2+3,{size:10,col:css('--matrix-row'),align:'right'});
    // intersection
    g.fillStyle = css('--matrix-cell');
    g.fillRect(cx-1.5, ry-1.5, Math.max(cw,3)+3, Math.max(ch,3)+3);
    txt(g,'x_ij', cx+Math.max(cw,3)+8, ry+3,{size:10,col:css('--matrix-cell'),weight:600});
  }

  // y bands to the right: lineage / batch / S score
  const bx = w-padR+14, bw=22;
  for(let r=0;r<mxRows.length;r++){
    const ci = mxRows[r];
    g.fillStyle = LINCOL[lineageOf[cellType[ci]]];
    g.fillRect(bx, padT+r*ch, bw, Math.max(ch,0.9));
    g.fillStyle = BATCHCOL[cellBatch[ci]%BATCHCOL.length];
    g.fillRect(bx+bw+5, padT+r*ch, bw, Math.max(ch,0.9));
    const s = sScore[ci];
    g.globalAlpha = s>0 ? Math.min(1,s/1.2) : 1;
    g.fillStyle = s>0 ? css('--series-6') : css('--line');
    g.fillRect(bx+2*(bw+5), padT+r*ch, bw, Math.max(ch,0.9));
    g.globalAlpha=1;
  }
  txt(g,'y →', bx-6, padT-11,{size:10,align:'right'});
  // the bands are only 22px wide, so these labels have to stay very short
  ['type','batch','S'].forEach((s,k)=> txt(g,s,bx+k*(bw+5)+bw/2, padT+mxRows.length*ch+13,{size:9.5,align:'center'}));
  line(g, bx-7, padT-4, bx-7, padT+mxRows.length*ch+4, css('--line2'),1);

  /* Readout only — the CLICK stays on the canvas's own exact floor-divide.
     PC.hover's hit radius has a 24px floor and this grid's row pitch is under
     2px, so routing the click through it would snap the selection across a
     dozen rows; the tooltip can tolerate that, a selection cannot. Points are
     the cell centres, indexed r*NCOL+c so the readout can name both axes. */
  const mxPts = [];
  for(let r=0;r<mxRows.length;r++)
    for(let c=0;c<NCOL;c++)
      mxPts.push([padL+c*cw+cw/2, padT+r*ch+ch/2, r*NCOL+c]);
  bindHover(cv, mxPts, k => {
    const r=Math.floor(k/NCOL), c=k%NCOL, ci=mxRows[r];
    if(ci==null) return '';
    return `<b>x<sub>ij</sub> = ${(MAT[ci*NCOL+c]/255).toFixed(3)}</b>`+
      `<br>row i · ${D.cells.barcodes[ci]}`+
      `<br>${D.cell_type_names[cellType[ci]]} · ${lineageOf[cellType[ci]]}`+
      `<br>col j · ${D.column_names[c]} (${D.column_kind[c]==='gene'?'gene':'protein'})`;
  });

  VIEWID('mx-shape').textContent =
    D.dataset.n_cells.toLocaleString()+' × '+(D.dataset.n_genes+D.dataset.n_proteins).toLocaleString();
  VIEWID('mx-cap').innerHTML =
    `Drawn here: a <b>${mxRows.length}</b> row × <b>${NCOL}</b> column display slice, sorted by cell type.
     The full matrix is ${D.dataset.n_cells.toLocaleString()} × ${(D.dataset.n_genes+D.dataset.n_proteins).toLocaleString()}.
     The three colour bands at the right edge are the labels <b>y</b> (cell type coloured by lineage, batch, S score); they are <b>not columns of X</b>.
     Clicking the heatmap changes the selected row and column at once.`;
}

function drawRow(){

  const cv = VIEWID('cv-row');
  const {g,w,h} = fit(cv);
  const i = state.cell, base=i*NCOL;
  const nGene = D.column_kind.filter(k=>k==='gene').length;
  const rowCol = css('--matrix-row');

  // top: this cell's strongest genes, taken from all 13,953
  const padT=16, barH=54;
  txt(g,'① The '+NTOP+' most strongly expressed genes in this cell (out of all '+D.dataset.n_genes.toLocaleString()+')',6,10,{size:10.5,col:rowCol,weight:600});
  // shared scale across all cells, so bar height is comparable cell to cell
  const gmax = D.top_genes.hi || 1;
  const bw=(w-14)/NTOP;
  txt(g,'shared scale 0 – '+gmax.toFixed(1),w-6,10,{size:9.5,align:'right'});
  for(let k=0;k<NTOP;k++){
    const v=topVal[i*NTOP+k], hh=(v/gmax)*barH;
    g.fillStyle=rowCol; g.globalAlpha=.82;
    g.fillRect(7+k*bw, padT+barH-hh, bw-2.5, hh);
    g.globalAlpha=1;
    g.save(); g.translate(7+k*bw+bw/2, padT+barH+3); g.rotate(-Math.PI/2.6);
    txt(g, D.gene_names_all[topIdx[i*NTOP+k]] || '', 0,0,{size:9,align:'right'});
    g.restore();
  }
  line(g,7,padT+barH,w-7,padT+barH,css('--line2'),1);
  // bottom: full 134-protein profile — same unit, so one shared scale is honest
  const py=h-64;
  txt(g,'② The full 134-protein profile (same unit, one shared scale)',6,py-8,{size:10.5,col:rowCol,weight:600});
  const pw=(w-14)/134;
  for(let c=0;c<134;c++){
    const v=MAT[base+nGene+c]/255, hh=v*46;
    g.fillStyle=rowCol; g.globalAlpha=.55+.45*v;
    g.fillRect(7+c*pw, py+46-hh, Math.max(pw-0.4,0.7), hh);
    g.globalAlpha=1;
  }
  // mark the selected column if it is a protein
  if(state.col>=nGene){
    const c=state.col-nGene;
    line(g,7+c*pw+pw/2, py-2, 7+c*pw+pw/2, py+50, css('--matrix-cell'),1.4);
  }
  line(g,7,py+46,w-7,py+46,css('--line2'),1);

  /* two point sets in one list: the NTOP gene bars (index k) and the 134 protein
     bars (index NTOP+c), so one hover covers both halves of the panel */
  const rowPts = [];
  for(let k=0;k<NTOP;k++)
    rowPts.push([7+k*bw+bw/2, padT+barH-(topVal[i*NTOP+k]/gmax)*barH, k]);
  for(let c2=0;c2<134;c2++)
    rowPts.push([7+c2*pw+pw/2, py+46-(MAT[base+nGene+c2]/255)*46, NTOP+c2]);
  bindHover(cv, rowPts, k => k<NTOP
    ? `<b>${D.gene_names_all[topIdx[i*NTOP+k]]}</b><br>gene · ${topVal[i*NTOP+k].toFixed(2)} (shared scale 0–${gmax.toFixed(1)})`
    : `<b>${D.column_names[nGene+(k-NTOP)]}</b><br>surface protein · ${(MAT[base+nGene+(k-NTOP)]/255).toFixed(3)}`);

  const ct = D.cell_type_names[cellType[i]];
  // most cells' strongest genes are housekeeping, which is the point worth making
  let nHouse=0;
  for(let k=0;k<NTOP;k++){
    const gname = D.gene_names_all[topIdx[i*NTOP+k]] || '';
    if(/^(MT-|RPL|RPS|MALAT1|EEF1A1|TMSB4X|ACTB|B2M)/.test(gname)) nHouse++;
  }
  VIEWID('row-cap').innerHTML =
    `Selected cell <span class="mono">${D.cells.barcodes[i]}</span> · true type <b>${ct}</b> ·
     batch <b>${D.batch_names[cellBatch[i]]}</b>${heldout[i]?' · <b>its label was never seen during training</b>':''}.
     <b>${nHouse}</b> of its ${NTOP} most strongly expressed genes are housekeeping genes, which most cells use heavily
     (mitochondrial, ribosomal, MALAT1 and similar). The most strongly expressed genes are not the most informative,
     which is why the model needs the SVD and the labels to find what separates cell types.`;
}

function drawCol(){

  const cv = VIEWID('cv-col');
  const {g,w,h} = fit(cv);
  const j = state.col, colCol = css('--matrix-column');
  const name = D.column_names[j], kind = D.column_kind[j];

  // group cells of the display sample by lineage, draw a strip per lineage
  const groups = {};
  D.lineage_order.forEach(l=>groups[l]=[]);
  for(let i=0;i<NC;i++) groups[lineageOf[cellType[i]]].push(MAT[i*NCOL+j]/255);

  const order = D.lineage_order.filter(l=>groups[l].length>2);
  const padL=74, padT=8, padB=18;
  const rh = (h-padT-padB)/order.length;
  order.forEach((l,k)=>{
    const vals = groups[l], y0 = padT+k*rh;
    txt(g,l,padL-7,y0+rh/2+3,{size:10.5,align:'right',col:LINCOL[l],weight:600});
    // jittered strip
    g.fillStyle=LINCOL[l];
    const step = Math.max(1, Math.floor(vals.length/260));
    for(let m=0;m<vals.length;m+=step){
      const x = padL+vals[m]*(w-padL-14);
      const yy = y0+rh*0.28+((m*2654435761)%1000)/1000*rh*0.44;
      g.globalAlpha=.30; g.fillRect(x,yy,1.6,1.6);
    }
    g.globalAlpha=1;
    // mean marker
    const mean = vals.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/vals.length;
    const mx = padL+mean*(w-padL-14);
    line(g,mx,y0+rh*0.18,mx,y0+rh*0.82,LINCOL[l],2);
  });
  // where does the selected cell sit?
  const v = MAT[state.cell*NCOL+j]/255;
  const xv = padL+v*(w-padL-14);
  line(g,xv,padT-2,xv,h-padB+2,css('--matrix-cell'),1.3);
  txt(g,'selected cell',xv+4,h-padB+13,{size:9.5,col:css('--matrix-cell')});
  line(g,padL,h-padB,w-14,h-padB,css('--line2'),1);
  txt(g,'0',padL,h-padB+13,{size:9.5});
  txt(g,'high →',w-14,h-padB+13,{size:9.5,align:'right'});

  /* one point per lineage, at its mean marker — the mean is what the panel is
     actually asserting, so that is what the readout names */
  bindHover(cv, order.map((l,k)=>{
      const vals=groups[l], mean=vals.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/vals.length;
      return [padL+mean*(w-padL-14), padT+k*rh+rh/2, k];
    }),
    k => { const l=order[k], vals=groups[l];
           const mean=vals.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/vals.length;
           return `<b>${l}</b><br>mean ${mean.toFixed(3)} of ${name}`+
                  `<br>${vals.length.toLocaleString()} cells in the display sample`; });

  VIEWID('col-cap').innerHTML =
    `Column j = <b>${name}</b> (${kind==='gene'?'gene mRNA':'surface protein'}).
     Each dot is one cell of the display sample, in its lineage's row; the short vertical bar is that lineage's mean,
     and the long line marks the selected cell. The further apart the lineage means, the better this column tells
     cell types apart, which is what lets the model recover cell type from X.`;
}

/* ================= STAGE 2: scree ================= */
function drawScree(){

  const cv=VIEWID('cv-scree'); const {g,w,h}=fit(cv);
  const evr=D.explained_variance_ratio, n=evr.length;
  const padL=42,padR=12,padT=24,padB=26;   // padT leaves a line for the axis caption
  const mx=Math.max(...evr);
  let cum=0; const cums=evr.map(v=>cum+=v);
  // bars
  const bw=(w-padL-padR)/n;
  for(let i=0;i<n;i++){
    const hh=(evr[i]/mx)*(h-padT-padB);
    g.fillStyle=css('--accent'); g.globalAlpha=.55;
    g.fillRect(padL+i*bw, h-padB-hh, Math.max(bw-0.5,0.8), hh);
  }
  g.globalAlpha=1;
  // cumulative line
  g.strokeStyle=css('--series-2'); g.lineWidth=1.8; g.beginPath();
  for(let i=0;i<n;i++){
    const x=padL+i*bw+bw/2, y=h-padB-(cums[i]/cums[n-1])*(h-padT-padB);
    i? g.lineTo(x,y): g.moveTo(x,y);
  }
  g.stroke();
  line(g,padL,h-padB,w-padR,h-padB,css('--line2'),1);
  line(g,padL,padT,padL,h-padB,css('--line2'),1);
  txt(g,'variance explained per component',padL,12,{size:9.5,align:'left'});
  txt(g,'PC1',padL+bw/2,h-padB+13,{size:9.5,align:'center'});
  txt(g,'PC100',w-padR,h-padB+13,{size:9.5,align:'right'});
  txt(g,'cumulative →',w-padR-4,12,{size:9.5,align:'right',col:css('--series-2')});
  bindHover(cv, evr.map((v,i)=>[padL+i*bw+bw/2, h-padB-(v/mx)*(h-padT-padB), i]),
    i => `<b>PC${i+1}</b><br>explains ${(evr[i]*100).toFixed(2)}% of GEX variance`+
         `<br>cumulative ${(cums[i]*100).toFixed(2)}% over ${i+1} component${i?'s':''}`);
  VIEWID('scree-cap').innerHTML =
    `Bars: the share of gene-expression variance each component explains; line: the running total. Hover a bar to read it.
     All 100 components together explain <b>${(D.dataset.svd_explained_variance*100).toFixed(1)}%</b>. Single-cell gene data
     are extremely sparse, and most of the remaining variance is sequencing noise, so here the reduction removes noise
     rather than compressing without loss.`;
}

/* ================= STAGE 3: latent blocks + training ================= */
function softmax(a){ const m=Math.max(...a); const e=a.map(v=>Math.exp(v-m)); const s=e.reduce((x,y)=>x+y,0); return e.map(v=>v/s); }
function drawLatent(){

  const cv=VIEWID('cv-latent'); const {g,w,h}=fit(cv);
  if(!LAT){ txt(g,'(latent data missing)',10,20); return; }
  const i=state.cell, L=D.latent_layout;
  const z=[]; for(let k=0;k<LATD;k++) z.push(LAT[i*LATD+k]);
  const padL=8,padR=8,padT=26,barH=64;
  const cw=(w-padL-padR)/LATD;
  const blocks=[
    ['cell_type', L.cell_type, css('--series-1'),        '45 dims · cell-type logits'],
    ['batch',     L.batch,     css('--series-2'),  '9 dims · batch logits'],
    ['cycle',     L.cycle,     css('--series-6'),'2 · S / G2M'],
    ['free',      L.free,      css('--muted'),    '5 · free'],
  ];
  const mx=Math.max(...z,1e-6);
  blocks.forEach(([key,[a,b],col,label])=>{
    for(let k=a;k<b;k++){
      const hh=(z[k]/mx)*barH;
      g.fillStyle=col; g.globalAlpha=.85;
      g.fillRect(padL+k*cw, padT+barH-hh, Math.max(cw-1,1), Math.max(hh,0.6));
      g.globalAlpha=1;
    }
    const x0=padL+a*cw, x1=padL+b*cw;
    line(g,x0,padT+barH+4,x1-1,padT+barH+4,col,2);
    txt(g,label,(x0+x1)/2, padT+barH+18,{size:10,align:'center',col,weight:600});
    line(g,x1-0.5,padT-6,x1-0.5,padT+barH+2,css('--line2'),1);
  });
  txt(g,'z ∈ R^'+LATD+'  (the latent vector of this cell)',padL,12,{size:11,weight:600,col:css('--ink2')});

  // readouts
  const ctL=z.slice(L.cell_type[0],L.cell_type[1]);
  const btL=z.slice(L.batch[0],L.batch[1]);
  const pCt=softmax(ctL), pBt=softmax(btL);
  let am=0; pCt.forEach((v,k)=>{ if(v>pCt[am]) am=k; });
  const trueCt=cellType[i], trueBt=cellBatch[i];
  const ent = -pBt.reduce((s,p)=> s + (p>0? p*Math.log(p):0), 0) / Math.log(pBt.length);

  const y=h-30;
  txt(g,`softmax over the first 45 → predicts "${D.cell_type_names[am]}" p=${pCt[am].toFixed(2)}   |   true "${D.cell_type_names[trueCt]}" ${am===trueCt?'✓':'✗'}`,
      padL,y,{size:11.5,col: am===trueCt? css('--good'):css('--critical'),weight:600});
  txt(g,`normalised entropy of the middle 9 = ${ent.toFixed(3)} (1.000 = all batches equally likely; true batch ${D.batch_names[trueBt]})   |   S=${sScore[i].toFixed(2)}  G2M=${gScore[i].toFixed(2)}`,
      padL,y+15,{size:11,col:css('--ink3')});

  /* one point per latent dimension, at the top of its bar; the readout names the
     addressed block the dimension belongs to, which is the whole point of the panel */
  const blockOf = k => {
    for(const [key,[a,b]] of Object.entries({cell_type:L.cell_type,batch:L.batch,cycle:L.cycle,free:L.free}))
      if(k>=a && k<b) return key.replace('_',' ');
    return '—';
  };
  bindHover(cv, z.map((v,k)=>[padL+k*cw+cw/2, padT+barH-(v/mx)*barH, k]),
    k => `<b>z[${k}] = ${z[k].toFixed(4)}</b><br>block: ${blockOf(k)}`+
         `<br>cell ${D.cells.barcodes[i]}`);
  VIEWID('latent-cap').innerHTML =
    `JAE in one sentence: <b>the first 45 numbers should peak</b> at the cell's type, <b>the middle 9 should be flat</b>
     (no batch stands out), the next 2 should track the cell cycle, and the last 5 have no target, left free for the
     network to use. Hover a bar to read its value.`;
}

function drawTrain(){

  const cv=VIEWID('cv-train'); const {g,w,h}=fit(cv);
  const t=D.training && D.training['jae_full'];
  if(!t || !t.curve || !t.curve.length){ txt(g,'(training curve missing)',10,20); return; }
  const c=t.curve, n=c.length;
  const padL=40,padR=62,padT=14,padB=26;   // padR holds the two series labels
  const X=i=>padL+(i/(n-1||1))*(w-padL-padR);
  const Y=v=>h-padB-v*(h-padT-padB);            // v in [0,1]
  // cell type accuracy (up = good)
  g.strokeStyle=css('--good'); g.lineWidth=1.9; g.beginPath();
  c.forEach((p,i)=> i? g.lineTo(X(i),Y(p.acc)) : g.moveTo(X(i),Y(p.acc)));
  g.stroke();
  // batch accuracy (should collapse to chance)
  g.strokeStyle=css('--series-2'); g.lineWidth=1.9; g.beginPath();
  c.forEach((p,i)=> i? g.lineTo(X(i),Y(p.bacc)) : g.moveTo(X(i),Y(p.bacc)));
  g.stroke();
  // chance line
  const chance=1/D.batch_names.length;
  g.setLineDash([3,3]); line(g,padL,Y(chance),w-padR,Y(chance),css('--ink3'),1); g.setLineDash([]);
  txt(g,'chance '+chance.toFixed(3), w-padR-3, Y(chance)-4,{size:9.5,align:'right'});
  // recon loss on the right axis
  const rmax=Math.max(...c.map(p=>p.r)), rmin=Math.min(...c.map(p=>p.r));
  g.strokeStyle=css('--accent'); g.lineWidth=1.4; g.setLineDash([4,3]); g.beginPath();
  c.forEach((p,i)=>{ const y=h-padB-((rmax-p.r)/(rmax-rmin||1))*(h-padT-padB); i?g.lineTo(X(i),y):g.moveTo(X(i),y);});
  g.stroke(); g.setLineDash([]);
  line(g,padL,h-padB,w-padR,h-padB,css('--line2'),1);
  line(g,padL,padT,padL,h-padB,css('--line2'),1);
  txt(g,'1.0',padL-5,padT+4,{size:9.5,align:'right'});
  txt(g,'0',padL-5,h-padB+3,{size:9.5,align:'right'});
  txt(g,'epoch',w-padR,h-padB+14,{size:9.5,align:'right'});
  txt(g,'cell type',X(n-1)+4,Y(c[n-1].acc)+3,{size:10,col:css('--good'),weight:600});
  txt(g,'batch',X(n-1)+4,Y(c[n-1].bacc)+3,{size:10,col:css('--series-2'),weight:600});
  /* one point per epoch, on the cell-type curve; the readout carries all three
     series so the reader does not have to hover each line separately */
  bindHover(cv, c.map((p,i)=>[X(i), Y(p.acc), i]),
    i => `<b>epoch ${i+1}</b> of ${n}<br>cell-type accuracy ${(c[i].acc*100).toFixed(1)}%`+
         `<br>batch accuracy ${(c[i].bacc*100).toFixed(1)}% (chance ${(chance*100).toFixed(1)}%)`+
         `<br>reconstruction loss ${c[i].r.toFixed(4)}`);
  const last=c[n-1];
  VIEWID('train-cap').innerHTML =
    `Solid lines: how often the cell-type block names the right type, and the batch block the right batch, after each
     epoch (one pass over the training cells). After ${n} epochs: cell-type accuracy <b>${(last.acc*100).toFixed(1)}%</b>,
     batch accuracy <b>${(last.bacc*100).toFixed(1)}%</b> (chance is ${(chance*100).toFixed(1)}%).
     The dashed line is the reconstruction loss, scaled to the chart height. Cell-type accuracy climbing while batch
     accuracy falls to chance shows the two label losses doing their separate jobs. Hover the chart to read each epoch.`;
}

/* ================= STAGE 4: metrics, trade-off, embedding ================= */
const METRIC_LABELS = [
  ['nmi','NMI','agreement between clusters and cell type','bio'],
  ['asw_cell_type','cell type ASW','are cell types well separated','bio'],
  ['cell_cycle_conservation','cell cycle cons.','did the cell-cycle signal survive','bio'],
  ['trajectory_conservation','trajectory cons.','did the erythroid trajectory survive','bio'],
  ['asw_batch','batch ASW','are batches mixed within a cell type','batch'],
  ['graph_connectivity','graph conn.','does each cell type stay in one piece','batch'],
];
function buildMetrics(){
  const tbl=VIEWID('tbl-metrics');
  const V=D.metrics.variants||{};
  const ours=V.jae_full;
  if(!ours){ tbl.innerHTML='<tbody><tr><td>metrics missing</td></tr></tbody>'; return; }
  let html='<thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>All cells</th><th>Held-out only</th><th>Rewards</th></tr></thead><tbody>';
  METRIC_LABELS.forEach(([k,label,desc,grp])=>{
    const a=ours.all[k], hd=ours.heldout[k];
    const gcol = grp==='bio' ? 'var(--series-1)' : 'var(--series-2)';
    const gtxt = grp==='bio' ? 'biology kept' : 'batch removed';
    html+=`<tr><td><b>${label}</b><br><span style="color:var(--ink3);font-size:11.5px">${desc}</span></td>`+
      `<td class="num">${a!=null?a.toFixed(4):'—'}</td>`+
      `<td class="num" style="color:var(--ink3)">${hd!=null?hd.toFixed(4):'—'}</td>`+
      `<td style="text-align:right;font-size:11.5px;color:${gcol}">${gtxt}</td></tr>`;
  });
  html+=`<tr class="hi"><td><b>Mean of the six</b></td>`+
    `<td class="num"><b>${ours.all.overall_mean_of_six.toFixed(4)}</b></td>`+
    `<td class="num" style="color:var(--ink3)">${ours.heldout.overall_mean_of_six.toFixed(4)}</td><td></td></tr>`;
  html+='</tbody>';
  tbl.innerHTML=html;

  const cfg=D.metrics.config||{};
  VIEWID('metrics-cap').innerHTML =
    `Higher is better for every metric. Four reward keeping biological structure, two reward removing batch effects,
     and the last row is their plain average. The first column scores all ${(cfg.n_cells||0).toLocaleString()} cells;
     the second only the ${(cfg.n_heldout||0).toLocaleString()} held-out cells, whose labels the model never saw.`;
}

function drawTradeoff(){

  const cv=VIEWID('cv-tradeoff'); const {g,w,h}=fit(cv);
  const V=D.metrics.variants||{};
  const pts=Object.keys(V).map(k=>({k,x:V[k].all.bio_conservation_mean,y:V[k].all.batch_removal_mean}))
                .filter(p=>isFinite(p.x)&&isFinite(p.y));
  if(!pts.length){ txt(g,'(metrics missing)',10,20); return; }
  const padL=44,padR=14,padT=14,padB=30;
  const xs=pts.map(p=>p.x), ys=pts.map(p=>p.y);
  const x0=Math.min(...xs)-.03, x1=Math.max(...xs)+.03;
  const y0=Math.min(...ys)-.03, y1=Math.max(...ys)+.03;
  const X=v=>padL+(v-x0)/(x1-x0||1)*(w-padL-padR);
  const Y=v=>h-padB-(v-y0)/(y1-y0||1)*(h-padT-padB);
  line(g,padL,h-padB,w-padR,h-padB,css('--line2'),1);
  line(g,padL,padT,padL,h-padB,css('--line2'),1);
  txt(g,'biological conservation (mean of 4) →',w-padR,h-padB+16,{size:10,align:'right'});
  g.save(); g.translate(12,padT+4); g.rotate(-Math.PI/2);
  txt(g,'← batch removal (mean of 2)',0,0,{size:10,align:'right'}); g.restore();
  txt(g,x0.toFixed(2),padL,h-padB+16,{size:9.5});
  txt(g,y1.toFixed(2),padL-5,padT+4,{size:9.5,align:'right'});
  pts.forEach(p=>{
    const cur = p.k===state.variant;
    g.beginPath(); g.arc(X(p.x),Y(p.y), cur?6:4.2, 0, Math.PI*2);
    g.fillStyle = cur? css('--accent') : css('--ink3');
    g.globalAlpha = cur? 1 : .55; g.fill(); g.globalAlpha=1;
    if(cur||p.k==='jae_full'||p.k==='svd61'||p.k==='ae_only')
      txt(g,p.k,X(p.x)+8,Y(p.y)+3.5,{size:10,col:css('--ink2'),weight:600});
  });
  /* every variant is a point; clicking one makes it the shown variant, which is
     the same thing the select above the embedding does */
  bindHover(cv, pts.map((p,i)=>[X(p.x), Y(p.y), i]),
    i => `<b>${pts[i].k}</b><br>biological conservation ${pts[i].x.toFixed(4)}`+
         `<br>batch removal ${pts[i].y.toFixed(4)}`+
         `<br>mean of six ${(V[pts[i].k].all.overall_mean_of_six).toFixed(4)}`,
    { onClick: i => { state.variant = pts[i].k;
                      const sv=VIEWID('sel-variant'); if(sv) sv.value=state.variant;
                      drawEmb(); drawTradeoff(); } });
}

/* ---- embedding scatter ---- */
const embGeom={};
function colorOfCell(i){
  switch(state.color){
    case 'lineage': return LINCOL[lineageOf[cellType[i]]];
    case 'celltype': { const t=cellType[i];
      const base=LINCOL[lineageOf[t]];
      return shade(base, ((t*47)%100)/100*0.5-0.25); }
    case 'batch': return BATCHCOL[cellBatch[i]%BATCHCOL.length];
    case 'cycle': { const v=Math.max(0,Math.min(1,(sScore[i]-D.cells.S.lo)/(D.cells.S.hi-D.cells.S.lo)));
      return PC.rampColor(0.18+0.82*v); }
    case 'pseudotime': { const v=pTime[i];
      if(v<0) return css('--line');
      return PC.rampColor(v); }
  }
  return css('--ink3');
}
function shade(hex,amt){
  const m=hex.match(/#(..)(..)(..)/); if(!m) return hex;
  let [r,gg,b]=[1,2,3].map(k=>parseInt(m[k],16));
  const f=v=>Math.max(0,Math.min(255,Math.round(v+amt*120)));
  return `rgb(${f(r)},${f(gg)},${f(b)})`;
}
function drawEmb(){

  const cv=VIEWID('cv-emb'); const {g,w,h}=fit(cv);
  const C=coordsOf(state.variant); if(!C){ txt(g,'(coordinates missing)',10,20); return; }
  const padL=10,padR=10,padT=10,padB=10;
  let x0=Infinity,x1=-Infinity,y0=Infinity,y1=-Infinity;
  for(let i=0;i<NC;i++){ x0=Math.min(x0,C.x[i]); x1=Math.max(x1,C.x[i]); y0=Math.min(y0,C.y[i]); y1=Math.max(y1,C.y[i]); }
  const sx=(w-padL-padR)/(x1-x0||1), sy=(h-padT-padB)/(y1-y0||1), s=Math.min(sx,sy);
  const ox=padL+((w-padL-padR)-(x1-x0)*s)/2, oy=padT+((h-padT-padB)-(y1-y0)*s)/2;
  embGeom.map = i => [ox+(C.x[i]-x0)*s, oy+(y1-C.y[i])*s];
  for(let i=0;i<NC;i++){
    if(state.lineage && lineageOf[cellType[i]]!==state.lineage) continue;
    const [px,py]=embGeom.map(i);
    g.fillStyle=colorOfCell(i); g.globalAlpha=.62;
    g.fillRect(px-1.1,py-1.1,2.2,2.2);
  }
  g.globalAlpha=1;
  const [cx,cy]=embGeom.map(state.cell);
  g.strokeStyle=css('--matrix-cell'); g.lineWidth=2;
  g.beginPath(); g.arc(cx,cy,7,0,Math.PI*2); g.stroke();
  line(g,cx-12,cy,cx-8,cy,css('--matrix-cell'),2); line(g,cx+8,cy,cx+12,cy,css('--matrix-cell'),2);

  /* THE SHARED HIT-TESTER. This panel used to carry its own nearest-point loop
     on `cve.onclick` with a `bd < 900` cutoff and no readout at all; the loop,
     the 30px radius and the lineage mask are all expressed here instead, so the
     panel now gains the tooltip every other plot in the suite has and stays on
     the shared path for anything PC.hover grows later. `mask` is a predicate, so
     a lineage filter no longer needs the draw loop's `continue`. */
  const embPts = new Array(NC);
  for(let i=0;i<NC;i++){ const [px,py]=embGeom.map(i); embPts[i]=[px,py,i]; }
  bindHover(cv, embPts, i =>
      `<b>${D.cells.barcodes[i]}</b><br>${D.cell_type_names[cellType[i]]}`+
      `<br>lineage ${lineageOf[cellType[i]]} · batch ${D.batch_names[cellBatch[i]]}`+
      `<br>S ${sScore[i].toFixed(2)} · G2M ${gScore[i].toFixed(2)}`+
      (heldout[i]? '<br>label held out' : ''),
    { radius: 30,
      mask: i => !state.lineage || lineageOf[cellType[i]]===state.lineage,
      onClick: i => setCell(i) });

  // legend
  const lg=VIEWID('emb-legend'); lg.innerHTML='';
  if(state.color==='lineage'||state.color==='celltype'){
    D.lineage_order.forEach(l=>{ lg.innerHTML+=`<span><i style="background:${LINCOL[l]}"></i>${l}</span>`; });
  } else if(state.color==='batch'){
    D.batch_names.forEach((b,k)=>{ lg.innerHTML+=`<span><i style="background:${BATCHCOL[k%BATCHCOL.length]}"></i>${b}</span>`; });
  } else if(state.color==='cycle'){
    lg.innerHTML=`<span><i style="background:${PC.rampColor(0.18)}"></i>low S score</span><span><i style="background:${PC.rampColor(1)}"></i>high S score</span>`;
  } else {
    lg.innerHTML=`<span><i style="background:${PC.rampColor(0)}"></i>early (HSC)</span><span><i style="background:${PC.rampColor(1)}"></i>late (reticulocyte)</span><span><i style="background:${css('--line')}"></i>no pseudotime (the other 39 cell types)</span>`;
  }
  const vt=D.training[state.variant];
  VIEWID('emb-cap').innerHTML =
    `Variant <b>${state.variant}</b>${vt&&vt.weights? ', loss weights <span class="mono">['+vt.weights.join(', ')+']</span>':''}.
     Each point is one cell (${NC.toLocaleString()} shown, sampled across cell types), placed by a UMAP of that
     variant's 61 numbers. Use Colour by and Variant to change the view; the lineage filter in the Design matrix
     section applies here too. Hover a point to identify it, and click it to select that cell here and in the
     Design matrix section. Maps of different variants are rotated or reflected to line up (orthogonal Procrustes);
     their shapes are unchanged.`;
}

function drawTrace(){

  const cv=VIEWID('cv-trace'); const {g,w,h}=fit(cv);
  const i=state.cell, nGene=D.column_kind.filter(k=>k==='gene').length;
  const pw=(w-14)/134;
  for(let c=0;c<134;c++){
    const v=MAT[i*NCOL+nGene+c]/255, hh=v*(h-34);
    g.fillStyle=LINCOL[lineageOf[cellType[i]]]; g.globalAlpha=.5+.5*v;
    g.fillRect(7+c*pw, h-22-hh, Math.max(pw-0.4,0.7), hh);
  }
  g.globalAlpha=1;
  line(g,7,h-22,w-7,h-22,css('--line2'),1);
  txt(g,'134 surface proteins of the selected cell',7,12,{size:10,col:css('--ink3')});
  // label the 3 strongest proteins
  const vals=[]; for(let c=0;c<134;c++) vals.push([MAT[i*NCOL+nGene+c],c]);
  vals.sort((a,b)=>b[0]-a[0]);
  vals.slice(0,3).forEach(([v,c])=>{
    txt(g, D.column_names[nGene+c], 7+c*pw+pw/2, h-8,{size:9,align:'center',col:css('--ink2')});
  });
  /* one point per surface protein */
  bindHover(cv, Array.from({length:134},(_,c)=>
      [7+c*pw+pw/2, h-22-(MAT[i*NCOL+nGene+c]/255)*(h-34), c]),
    c => `<b>${D.column_names[nGene+c]}</b><br>surface protein · ${(MAT[i*NCOL+nGene+c]/255).toFixed(3)}`+
         `<br>cell ${D.cells.barcodes[i]}`);
  const ct=D.cell_type_names[cellType[i]];
  VIEWID('trace-cap').innerHTML =
    `Every point on the map is <b>one real cell</b>: here are its barcode, batch, annotated cell type and strongest
     genes, and the bars show its 134 surface-protein values (the three largest are labelled; hover a bar to read it).`;
  const kv=VIEWID('kv-cell');
  const topG=[]; for(let k=0;k<Math.min(5,NTOP);k++) topG.push(D.gene_names_all[topIdx[i*NTOP+k]]);
  kv.innerHTML =
    `<dt>barcode</dt><dd style="font-size:11px">${D.cells.barcodes[i]}</dd>`+
    `<dt>true type</dt><dd>${ct}</dd>`+
    `<dt>lineage</dt><dd style="color:${LINCOL[lineageOf[cellType[i]]]}">${lineageOf[cellType[i]]}</dd>`+
    `<dt>batch</dt><dd>${D.batch_names[cellBatch[i]]}</dd>`+
    `<dt>S / G2M</dt><dd>${sScore[i].toFixed(2)} / ${gScore[i].toFixed(2)}</dd>`+
    `<dt>erythroid pseudotime</dt><dd>${pTime[i]<0?'not applicable':pTime[i].toFixed(3)}</dd>`+
    `<dt>strongest genes</dt><dd style="font-size:11.5px">${topG.join(', ')}</dd>`+
    `<dt>training label</dt><dd>${heldout[i]?'held out (never trained on)':'training set'}</dd>`;
}

/* ================= static fills ================= */
function fillStatics(){
  const d=D.dataset;
  const set=(id,v)=>{const e=VIEWID(id); if(e) e.textContent=v;};
  set('f-cells', d.n_cells.toLocaleString()); set('f-cells3', d.n_cells.toLocaleString());
  set('f-cells4', d.n_cells.toLocaleString());
  set('f-genes', d.n_genes.toLocaleString()); set('f-genes2', d.n_genes.toLocaleString());
  set('f-genes3', d.n_genes.toLocaleString());
  set('f-prot', d.n_proteins);
  set('f-negfrac', (D.neg_fraction!=null? (D.neg_fraction*100).toFixed(0):'21')+'%');

  VIEWID('kv-x').innerHTML =
    `<dt>one sample</dt><dd>one bone-marrow cell</dd>`+
    `<dt>GEX</dt><dd>${d.n_genes.toLocaleString()} gene counts</dd>`+
    `<dt>ADT</dt><dd>${d.n_proteins} protein counts</dd>`+
    `<dt>shape of X</dt><dd>${d.n_cells.toLocaleString()} × ${(d.n_genes+d.n_proteins).toLocaleString()}</dd>`;
  VIEWID('kv-y').innerHTML =
    `<dt>cell type</dt><dd>${d.n_cell_types} types, annotated by hand</dd>`+
    `<dt>batch</dt><dd>${d.n_batches} site × donor</dd>`+
    `<dt>cell cycle</dt><dd>continuous S / G2M scores</dd>`+
    `<dt>pseudotime</dt><dd>erythroid only, 10,373 cells</dd>`;

  const cc=d.cell_cycle||{};
  VIEWID('kv-repro').innerHTML =
    `<dt>data</dt><dd>GEO GSE194122 / openproblems S3</dd>`+
    `<dt>SVD seed</dt><dd>123, 100 components</dd>`+
    `<dt>train / val split</dt><dd>90/10, seed 42</dd>`+
    `<dt>display sample</dt><dd>${NC.toLocaleString()} cells, stratified, seed 7</dd>`+
    `<dt>cycle genes matched</dt><dd>${cc.s_genes_used||43} S + ${cc.g2m_genes_used||54} G2M / 97</dd>`+
    `<dt>analysis saved</dt><dd>${D.generated}</dd>`;

  const div=D.metrics.divergences_from_scib||{};
  const nDiv=Object.keys(div).length;
  const sub=(D.metrics.config&&D.metrics.config.subsample)||8000;
  VIEWID('honesty').innerHTML =
    `<b>How the six metrics are computed.</b>
     They follow the definitions of the <span class="mono">scib</span> benchmarking package, reimplemented with
     numpy and scikit-learn. The main differences: NMI runs KMeans over a range of <span class="mono">k</span>
     instead of tuning Louvain resolution; trajectory conservation uses distances along a nearest-neighbour graph
     instead of diffusion pseudotime; and the silhouette-based metrics use a stratified subsample of
     ${sub.toLocaleString()} cells.
     ${nDiv? 'All '+nDiv+' metrics differ from scib in implementation; the Source evidence section lists each difference.':''}`;

  const ccMix = cc.our_phase_mix||{}, dsMix = cc.dataset_phase_mix||{};
  const pct = (m,k) => {
    const tot = Object.values(m).reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0);
    return tot? (m[k]/tot*100).toFixed(0)+'%' : '—';
  };
}

/* ================= wiring ================= */
function redrawAll(){
  drawMatrix(); drawRow(); drawCol(); drawScree();
  drawLatent(); drawTrain(); drawTradeoff(); drawEmb(); drawTrace();
}
function setCell(i){ state.cell=i; drawMatrix(); drawRow(); drawCol(); drawLatent(); drawEmb(); drawTrace(); }
function setCol(j){ state.col=j; drawMatrix(); drawRow(); drawCol(); }

function init(){
  fillStatics();
  // column selector
  const sc=VIEWID('sel-col');
  D.column_names.forEach((n,j)=>{
    const o=document.createElement('option'); o.value=j;
    o.textContent=(D.column_kind[j]==='gene'?'gene · ':'protein · ')+n; sc.appendChild(o);
  });
  // default to a gene with obvious lineage structure
  const dflt=D.column_names.indexOf('CD3E'); state.col = dflt>=0? dflt : 0;
  sc.value=state.col;
  sc.onchange=()=> setCol(+sc.value);

  const sl=VIEWID('sel-lin');
  D.lineage_order.forEach(l=>{ const o=document.createElement('option'); o.value=l; o.textContent=l; sl.appendChild(o); });
  sl.onchange=()=>{ state.lineage=sl.value; redrawAll(); };

  const sv=VIEWID('sel-variant');
  Object.keys(D.coords).forEach(v=>{ const o=document.createElement('option'); o.value=v; o.textContent=v; sv.appendChild(o); });
  sv.value = D.coords['jae_full']? 'jae_full' : Object.keys(D.coords)[0];
  state.variant=sv.value;
  sv.onchange=()=>{ state.variant=sv.value; drawEmb(); drawTradeoff(); };

  VIEWROOT.querySelectorAll('[data-color]').forEach(b=>{
    b.onclick=()=>{
      VIEWROOT.querySelectorAll('[data-color]').forEach(x=>x.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false'));
      b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true');
      state.color=b.dataset.color; drawEmb();
    };
  });
  VIEWID('btn-random').onclick=()=>{
    let pool=[]; for(let i=0;i<NC;i++) if(!state.lineage||lineageOf[cellType[i]]===state.lineage) pool.push(i);
    if(pool.length) setCell(pool[Math.floor(Math.random()*pool.length)]);
  };

  // click interactions
  const cvm=VIEWID('cv-matrix');
  cvm.onclick=e=>{
    const r=cvm.getBoundingClientRect();
    const x=e.clientX-r.left, y=e.clientY-r.top;
    const c=Math.floor((x-mxGeom.padL)/mxGeom.cw);
    const rr=Math.floor((y-mxGeom.padT)/mxGeom.ch);
    if(c>=0&&c<NCOL){ state.col=c; VIEWID('sel-col').value=c; }
    if(rr>=0&&rr<mxRows.length) state.cell=mxRows[rr];
    drawMatrix(); drawRow(); drawCol(); drawLatent(); drawEmb(); drawTrace();
  };
  const cve=VIEWID('cv-emb');
  /* The nearest-point click this canvas used to own now lives in drawEmb()'s
     PC.hover call (radius 30 = the old `bd < 900`, same lineage mask, same
     setCell). The property handler is nulled rather than left in place, because
     it would double-fire alongside the shared one. */
  cve.onclick=null;
  cvm.tabIndex=0; cve.tabIndex=0;
  cve.onkeydown=e=>{ if(e.key==='Enter'||e.key===' '){ e.preventDefault(); VIEWID('btn-random').click(); } };

  buildMetrics();
  // pick an interesting starting cell: a myeloid cell the model never saw labelled
  let start=0;
  for(let i=0;i<NC;i++){ if(lineageOf[cellType[i]]==='Myeloid' && heldout[i]){ start=i; break; } }
  state.cell=start;
  redrawAll();
}

/* The ?theme= stamp goes through the shared writer instead of a hand-rolled
   setAttribute. It stays here rather than being deleted outright because this
   view paints before the suite script installs PC.initTheme, and a canvas drawn
   under the wrong palette would only correct itself on the next redraw. The
   other three contract pieces (toggle, matchMedia, MutationObserver) are
   initTheme's alone — this view hand-rolls none of them. */
const q=new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('theme');
if(q==='dark'||q==='light') document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme",q);

window.addEventListener('resize', ()=>{ clearTimeout(window._rt_explorer); window._rt_explorer=setTimeout(redrawAll,120); });
init();
window.__JAE_VIEWS__['explorer'] = (typeof redrawAll === 'function') ? redrawAll : function(){};
})();

/* ===== view: lab (from template_lab.html) ===== */
(function(){
var VIEWROOT = document.getElementById('view-lab');
var VIEWID = function(id){ return VIEWROOT.querySelector('#' + id) || document.getElementById('explorer-reference').querySelector('#' + id); };
const DATA = window.__JAE_PAYLOAD__;
const D = DATA;

function unb64(s,T){const b=atob(s);const buf=new ArrayBuffer(b.length);const v=new Uint8Array(buf);
  for(let i=0;i<b.length;i++)v[i]=b.charCodeAt(i);return new T(buf);}
function deq(c,lo,hi,mx){const o=new Float32Array(c.length);const s=(hi-lo)/mx;
  for(let i=0;i<c.length;i++)o[i]=lo+c[i]*s;return o;}
const css=n=>PC.css(n);

const NC=D.cells.n;
const cellType=unb64(D.cells.cell_type,Uint8Array);
const cellBatch=unb64(D.cells.batch,Uint8Array);
const sScore=deq(unb64(D.cells.S.data,Uint16Array),D.cells.S.lo,D.cells.S.hi,65535);
const lineageOf=D.cell_type_lineage;
const LINEAGE_TOKEN=['--series-1','--series-3','--series-5','--series-2',
                    '--series-6','--series-4','--muted'];
const LINCOL={};
function refreshLineageColours(){
  D.lineage_order.forEach((l,k)=>LINCOL[l]=css(LINEAGE_TOKEN[k%LINEAGE_TOKEN.length]));
}
refreshLineageColours();
const BATCH_TOKEN=['--series-1','--series-2','--series-3','--series-4','--series-5',
                  '--series-6','--series-7','--series-8','--muted'];
let BATCHCOL=[];
function refreshBatchColours(){ BATCHCOL=BATCH_TOKEN.map(css); }
refreshBatchColours();

const cache={};
function coordsOf(v){
  if(cache[v])return cache[v];
  const c=D.coords[v]; if(!c)return null;
  return cache[v]={x:deq(unb64(c.x,Uint16Array),c.sx[0],c.sx[1],65535),
                   y:deq(unb64(c.y,Uint16Array),c.sy[0],c.sy[1],65535)};
}
let COLOR='batch';
function colorOf(i){
  if(COLOR==='batch') return BATCHCOL[cellBatch[i]%BATCHCOL.length];
  if(COLOR==='lineage') return LINCOL[lineageOf[cellType[i]]];
  const v=Math.max(0,Math.min(1,(sScore[i]-D.cells.S.lo)/(D.cells.S.hi-D.cells.S.lo)));
  return PC.rampColor(0.15+0.85*v);
}
/* Sizing through the shared PC.fit, exactly as the explorer view does — see the
   long note there for the cached authored height and the cleared inline width. */
function fit(cv){
  const h = cv.__pcCssH !== undefined ? cv.__pcCssH
          : (cv.__pcCssH = +cv.getAttribute('height'));
  cv.style.width = "";
  const w = cv.clientWidth || (cv.parentElement && cv.parentElement.clientWidth) || 220;
  const g = PC.fit(cv, w, h);
  return {g,w,h};
}
function bindHover(cv, pts, html, opts){
  return PC.hover(cv, pts, Object.assign({
    onHit: (i, evt) => PC.tip(html(i), evt),
    onLeave: () => PC.hideTip()
  }, opts || {}));
}
function txt(g,s,x,y,{size=11,col=null,align='left',weight=400}={}){
  g.fillStyle=col||css('--ink3');
  g.font=weight+' '+size+'px '+PC.font.family();
  g.textAlign=align; g.textBaseline='alphabetic'; g.fillText(s,x,y);
}

/* shared extent across every small multiple, so panels really are comparable */
let EXT=null;
function extent(){
  if(EXT) return EXT;
  let x0=Infinity,x1=-Infinity,y0=Infinity,y1=-Infinity;
  Object.keys(D.coords).forEach(v=>{
    const C=coordsOf(v);
    for(let i=0;i<NC;i++){x0=Math.min(x0,C.x[i]);x1=Math.max(x1,C.x[i]);
      y0=Math.min(y0,C.y[i]);y1=Math.max(y1,C.y[i]);}
  });
  return EXT={x0,x1,y0,y1};
}
function drawMini(cv,variant){
  const {g,w,h}=fit(cv);
  const C=coordsOf(variant);
  if(!C){ txt(g,'('+variant+' missing)',8,18); return; }
  const e=extent();
  const s=Math.min(w/(e.x1-e.x0||1), h/(e.y1-e.y0||1))*0.94;
  const ox=(w-(e.x1-e.x0)*s)/2, oy=(h-(e.y1-e.y0)*s)/2;
  const pts=new Array(NC);
  for(let i=0;i<NC;i++){
    const px=ox+(C.x[i]-e.x0)*s, py=oy+(e.y1-C.y[i])*s;
    pts[i]=[px,py,i];
    g.fillStyle=colorOf(i); g.globalAlpha=.55;
    g.fillRect(px-.9,py-.9,1.8,1.8);
  }
  g.globalAlpha=1;
  /* every small multiple gets the same readout, and it names the VARIANT as well
     as the cell — the whole point of the panel is comparing variants, so the
     reader needs to know which one is under the pointer */
  bindHover(cv, pts, i =>
    `<b>${variant}</b><br>${D.cells.barcodes[i]}`+
    `<br>${lineageOf[cellType[i]]} · batch ${D.batch_names[cellBatch[i]]}`+
    `<br>S score ${sScore[i].toFixed(2)}`);
}

const METRICS=[
  ['nmi','NMI'],['asw_cell_type','type ASW'],['cell_cycle_conservation','cycle cons.'],
  ['trajectory_conservation','traj. cons.'],['asw_batch','batch ASW'],['graph_connectivity','graph conn.'],
];
const V=()=>D.metrics.variants||{};
function num(x,d=3){return x==null||!isFinite(x)?'—':(+x).toFixed(d);}

function panelHTML(v,title,meta,mark){
  return `<div class="panel${mark?' on':''}"><h4>${title}</h4><div class="meta">${meta}</div>
    <canvas height="168" data-variant="${v}" role="img" aria-label="Embedding projection for ${title}"></canvas></div>`;
}
function metricTable(variants, scope='all'){
  let html='<thead><tr><th>Variant</th>';
  METRICS.forEach(([,l])=>html+=`<th>${l}</th>`);
  html+='<th>bio mean</th><th>batch mean</th><th>mean of 6</th><th>cell-type acc.</th></tr></thead><tbody>';
  variants.forEach(({key,label,mark})=>{
    const e=V()[key]; if(!e) return;
    const s=e[scope];
    const tr=D.training[key]||{};
    const acc=tr.curve&&tr.curve.length? tr.curve[tr.curve.length-1].acc : null;
    html+=`<tr${mark?' class="hi"':''}><td><b>${label}</b><br><span class="mono" style="color:var(--ink3);font-size:11px">${key}</span></td>`;
    METRICS.forEach(([k])=>html+=`<td class="num">${num(s[k])}</td>`);
    html+=`<td class="num">${num(s.bio_conservation_mean)}</td><td class="num">${num(s.batch_removal_mean)}</td>`+
      `<td class="num"><b>${num(s.overall_mean_of_six)}</b></td>`+
      `<td class="num" style="color:var(--ink3)">${acc==null?'—':(acc*100).toFixed(1)+'%'}</td></tr>`;
  });
  return html+'</tbody>';
}

/* ---------- experiment definitions ---------- */
const EXP = {
  e1: {
    variants:[
      {key:'jae_batch0',  label:'λ_batch = 0',    meta:'[0.7, 0.2, 0.00, 0.05]'},
      {key:'jae_full',    label:'λ_batch = 0.05', meta:'[0.7, 0.2, 0.05, 0.05] ← paper', mark:true},
      {key:'jae_batch20', label:'λ_batch = 0.2',  meta:'[0.7, 0.2, 0.20, 0.05]'},
      {key:'jae_batch50', label:'λ_batch = 0.5',  meta:'[0.7, 0.2, 0.50, 0.05]'},
    ],
    cap(){
      const g=k=>V()[k]&&V()[k].all;
      const a=g('jae_batch0'), b=g('jae_full'), c=g('jae_batch50');
      if(!a||!b||!c) return '';
      return `Going from λ<sub>batch</sub>=0 to 0.5, the batch-removal mean moves from <b>${num(a.batch_removal_mean)}</b>
        to <b>${num(c.batch_removal_mean)}</b> while the biological-conservation mean moves from
        <b>${num(a.bio_conservation_mean)}</b> to <b>${num(c.bio_conservation_mean)}</b>. The paper's 0.05 sits at
        <b>${num(b.batch_removal_mean)} / ${num(b.bio_conservation_mean)}</b>.
        Compare these gaps with the seed-to-seed spread in Experiment 6.`;
    }
  },
  e2: {
    variants:[
      {key:'svd61',       label:'① No training at all', meta:'TruncatedSVD to the same 61 dims'},
      {key:'ae_only',     label:'② Plain autoencoder',  meta:'[1.0, 0.0, 0.00, 0.00]'},
      {key:'ae_celltype', label:'③ + cell type',        meta:'[0.7, 0.3, 0.00, 0.00]'},
      {key:'jae_full',    label:'④ Full JAE',           meta:'[0.7, 0.2, 0.05, 0.05]', mark:true},
    ],
    cap(){
      const g=k=>V()[k]&&V()[k].all;
      const s=g('svd61'), a=g('ae_only'), c=g('ae_celltype'), f=g('jae_full');
      if(!s||!a||!c||!f) return '';
      const t=k=>{const tr=D.training[k]; return tr&&tr.curve&&tr.curve.length? (tr.curve[tr.curve.length-1].acc*100).toFixed(1)+'%':'—';};
      return `First, the accuracy of reading cell type off an argmax over the first 45 dimensions: the plain
        autoencoder manages only <b>${t('ae_only')}</b> (nothing asked those dimensions to represent type, so it
        should be near the ${(100/D.cell_type_names.length).toFixed(1)}% chance level), rising to
        <b>${t('ae_celltype')}</b> once type supervision is added, and <b>${t('jae_full')}</b> for the full JAE.
        No surprise there.
        <br><br><b>The surprise is the NMI column (agreement between clusters and cell types): ${num(s.nmi)} → ${num(a.nmi)} → ${num(c.nmi)} → ${num(f.nmi)}.</b>
        The plain autoencoder (${num(a.nmi)}) is <b>worse than not training at all</b> (${num(s.nmi)}).
        A 61-dimensional bottleneck optimised purely for reconstruction does not organise cell-type structure
        better — it actually scrambles structure the SVD already had (remember the output ReLU truncates half
        the directions; see experiment 5). Only once type supervision is added does NMI jump to ${num(c.nmi)}.
        <br><br>So the conclusion here is not "labels are the icing on the cake". It is:
        <b>in this architecture, the readable cell-type structure in the latent space comes mainly from the
        labels, not from the reconstruction loss.</b>`;
    }
  },
  e3: {
    variants:[
      {key:'jae_full',              label:'Push toward uniform (what JAE does)', meta:'CE(z[45:54], uniform)', mark:true},
      {key:'jae_batch_supervised',  label:'Classify the batch correctly (control)', meta:'CE(z[45:54], true batch)'},
    ],
    cap(){
      const a=V()['jae_full'], b=V()['jae_batch_supervised'];
      if(!a||!b) return '';
      const ta=D.training['jae_full'], tb=D.training['jae_batch_supervised'];
      const ba=ta&&ta.curve.length? (ta.curve[ta.curve.length-1].bacc*100).toFixed(1)+'%':'—';
      const bb=tb&&tb.curve.length? (tb.curve[tb.curve.length-1].bacc*100).toFixed(1)+'%':'—';
      const chance=(100/D.batch_names.length).toFixed(1)+'%';
      return `Batch classification accuracy: <b>${ba}</b> with the uniform target versus <b>${bb}</b> with the
        classify-correctly target (chance is ${chance}). Batch-removal score:
        <b>${num(a.all.batch_removal_mean)}</b> versus <b>${num(b.all.batch_removal_mean)}</b>.
        That confirms the mechanism: <b>it is the target distribution of the loss, not the mere presence of a
        batch term, that does the batch correction</b>. Switch to classifying correctly and those 9 dimensions
        become a high-fidelity encoder of batch identity — precisely what we were trying to avoid.`;
    }
  },
  e4: {
    variants:[
      {key:'jae_gex_only', label:'GEX only', meta:'134 protein dims zeroed'},
      {key:'jae_adt_only', label:'ADT only', meta:'100 GEX SVD dims zeroed'},
      {key:'jae_full',     label:'GEX + ADT jointly', meta:'all 234 dims visible', mark:true},
    ],
    cap(){
      const g=k=>V()[k]&&V()[k].all;
      const a=g('jae_gex_only'), b=g('jae_adt_only'), f=g('jae_full');
      if(!a||!b||!f) return '';
      const trajBest = f.trajectory_conservation>=Math.max(a.trajectory_conservation,b.trajectory_conservation);
      return `Mean of six: GEX only <b>${num(a.overall_mean_of_six)}</b>, ADT only <b>${num(b.overall_mean_of_six)}</b>,
        joint <b>${num(f.overall_mean_of_six)}</b>. But look per metric rather than at the total:
        cell-type ASW favours ${a.asw_cell_type>b.asw_cell_type?'GEX':'ADT'}, while cycle conservation favours
        ${a.cell_cycle_conservation>b.cell_cycle_conservation?'GEX':'ADT'}.
        ${trajBest? '' : `<b>And trajectory conservation is actually highest for GEX alone
        (${num(a.trajectory_conservation)}) rather than the joint model (${num(f.trajectory_conservation)})</b> —
        adding a modality does not improve every metric monotonically.`}
        The two modalities carry information that does not fully overlap, which is both the point of "joint"
        and its cost.`;
    }
  },
  e5: {
    variants:[
      {key:'jae_full',       label:'As upstream (ReLU output)', meta:'encoder/decoder last layer = ReLU', mark:true},
      {key:'jae_linear_out', label:'Both ReLUs removed',        meta:'encoder/decoder last layer = linear'},
    ],
    cap(){
      const a=V()['jae_full'], b=V()['jae_linear_out'];
      if(!a||!b) return '';
      const d=b.all.overall_mean_of_six-a.all.overall_mean_of_six;
      return `Mean of six: <b>${num(a.all.overall_mean_of_six)}</b> (as upstream) versus
        <b>${num(b.all.overall_mean_of_six)}</b> (ReLUs removed), a difference of
        <b style="color:${d>0?'var(--good)':'var(--critical)'}">${d>0?'+':''}${num(d)}</b>.
        Cycle conservation alone: ${num(a.all.cell_cycle_conservation)} → ${num(b.all.cell_cycle_conservation)}.
        <b>A question raised by reading the source code is settled by a controlled experiment.</b>`;
    }
  },
  e6: {
    variants:[
      {key:'jae_full',       label:'Seed 0', meta:'torch.manual_seed(0)', mark:true},
      {key:'jae_full_seed1', label:'Seed 1', meta:'torch.manual_seed(1)'},
      {key:'jae_full_seed2', label:'Seed 2', meta:'torch.manual_seed(2)'},
    ],
    cap(){
      const ks=['jae_full','jae_full_seed1','jae_full_seed2'].filter(k=>V()[k]);
      if(ks.length<2) return '';
      const vals=ks.map(k=>V()[k].all.overall_mean_of_six);
      const mn=Math.min(...vals), mx=Math.max(...vals);
      const spread=mx-mn;
      const per=METRICS.map(([k,l])=>{
        const v=ks.map(kk=>V()[kk].all[k]);
        return l+' ±'+num((Math.max(...v)-Math.min(...v))/2,3);
      }).join(', ');
      return `The three seeds land between <b>${num(mn)}</b> and <b>${num(mx)}</b> on the mean of six, a spread of
        <b>${num(spread)}</b>. Half-ranges per metric: ${per}.
        <b>Differences in the mean of six smaller than about ${num(spread,3)} are within seed-to-seed variation.</b>`;
    }
  },
};

function renderExp(id){
  const e=EXP[id];
  VIEWID('m-'+id).innerHTML =
    e.variants.map(v=>panelHTML(v.key,v.label,v.meta,v.mark)).join('');
  VIEWID('t-'+id).innerHTML = metricTable(e.variants,'all');
  VIEWID('c-'+id).innerHTML = e.cap()||'';
}
function drawAllMinis(){
  VIEWROOT.querySelectorAll('canvas[data-variant]').forEach(cv=>drawMini(cv,cv.dataset.variant));
}
function renderGlobalLegend(){
  const lg=VIEWID('global-legend'); lg.innerHTML='';
  if(COLOR==='batch') D.batch_names.forEach((b,k)=>
    lg.innerHTML+=`<span><i style="background:${BATCHCOL[k%BATCHCOL.length]}"></i>${b}</span>`);
  else if(COLOR==='lineage') D.lineage_order.forEach(l=>
    lg.innerHTML+=`<span><i style="background:${LINCOL[l]}"></i>${l}</span>`);
  else lg.innerHTML=`<span><i style="background:${PC.rampColor(0.15)}"></i>low S</span><span><i style="background:${PC.rampColor(1)}"></i>high S</span>`;
}

let SCOPE='all';
function renderAllTable(){
  const order=['svd61','ae_only','ae_celltype','jae_batch0','jae_full','jae_batch20','jae_batch50',
               'jae_batch_supervised','jae_gex_only','jae_adt_only','jae_linear_out',
               'jae_full_seed1','jae_full_seed2','jae_full_faithful'];
  const labels={svd61:'No training · SVD to 61 dims',ae_only:'Plain autoencoder',ae_celltype:'AE + cell type',
    jae_batch0:'JAE λ_batch=0',jae_full:'Full JAE (paper config)',jae_batch20:'JAE λ_batch=0.2',
    jae_batch50:'JAE λ_batch=0.5',jae_batch_supervised:'Batch term classifies correctly',
    jae_gex_only:'GEX only',jae_adt_only:'ADT only',jae_linear_out:'Output ReLUs removed',
    jae_full_seed1:'Full JAE · seed 1',jae_full_seed2:'Full JAE · seed 2',
    jae_full_faithful:'Upstream hyperparameters, batch=32 lr=1e-4'};
  const list=order.filter(k=>V()[k]).map(k=>({key:k,label:labels[k]||k,mark:k==='jae_full'}));
  VIEWID('t-all').innerHTML=metricTable(list,SCOPE);
  const cfg=D.metrics.config||{};
  VIEWID('c-all').innerHTML =
    SCOPE==='all'
      ? `Scored on all ${(cfg.n_cells||0).toLocaleString()} cells, including those whose labels the model trained on.
         Click “Held-out 10% only” to score only the cells it never saw.`
      : `Scored on the ${(cfg.n_heldout||0).toLocaleString()} held-out cells only, whose labels the model never saw.
         Most variants score lower here and some score higher: this scope also has fewer cells
         (${(cfg.n_heldout||0).toLocaleString()} instead of ${(cfg.n_cells||0).toLocaleString()}), and metrics such as NMI
         and graph connectivity change with the number of cells.`;
  const div=D.metrics.divergences_from_scib||{};
  VIEWID('controls-note').innerHTML =
    `<b>What every variant shares.</b>
     The data, the train/validation split (seed 42), the architecture, the optimiser, batch size,
     learning rate, the early-stopping rule, the UMAP parameters and seed, and the metric implementations and
     their sampling seed.<br>
     The one exception is <span class="mono">jae_full_faithful</span>, which uses the upstream batch size and
     learning rate (batch 32, learning rate 1e-4) and so changes two factors at once; it is not part of any
     experiment above.`;
}

/* ---------- init ---------- */
function init(){
  const nf=VIEWID('f-neg');
  if(nf) nf.textContent = D.neg_fraction!=null? (D.neg_fraction*100).toFixed(0)+'%' : '21%';
  const nvar=Object.keys(V()).length || Object.keys(D.coords).length;
  VIEWID('f-nvar').textContent=nvar;
  VIEWID('f-nvar2').textContent=nvar;
  ['e1','e2','e3','e4','e5','e6'].forEach(renderExp);
  renderAllTable();
  renderGlobalLegend();
  drawAllMinis();

  VIEWROOT.querySelectorAll('[data-color]').forEach(b=>{
    b.onclick=()=>{
      VIEWROOT.querySelectorAll('[data-color]').forEach(x=>x.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false'));
      b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true');
      COLOR=b.dataset.color; renderGlobalLegend(); drawAllMinis();
    };
  });
  VIEWROOT.querySelectorAll('[data-scope]').forEach(b=>{
    b.onclick=()=>{
      VIEWROOT.querySelectorAll('[data-scope]').forEach(x=>x.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false'));
      b.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true');
      SCOPE=b.dataset.scope; renderAllTable();
    };
  });
}
/* through the shared writer; see the note in the explorer view above */
const q=new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('theme');
if(q==='dark'||q==='light') document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme",q);
window.addEventListener('resize',()=>{clearTimeout(window._rt_lab);window._rt_lab=setTimeout(drawAllMinis,120);});
init();
window.__JAE_VIEWS__['lab'] = (typeof drawAllMinis === 'function') ? drawAllMinis : function(){};
})();

PC.panels.dag.create(document.getElementById('workflowDag'),D.dag.steps,D.dag.options);
PC.registerRepaint(()=>{window.__JAE_VIEWS__.explorer();window.__JAE_VIEWS__.lab();});PC.repaint('initial',document);
